title: 10 for $10 Doesn't Mean Buy 10
editorialNotes: Final slide carries "Link in bio." verbatim from the script; no link is live in the setup phase, so Gate 6 CTA-reality applies.

copy.headline: "10 for $10" does not require you to buy 10.
Most stores honor the per-unit price regardless of quantity.
items: But the sign is designed to anchor you at 10.
Anchoring is one of the most studied effects in pricing psychology.

copy.headline: End-cap displays aren't curated deals. They're paid advertisements.
copy.body: Brands pay premium placement fees to sit at the end of the aisle where foot traffic is highest.

copy.headline: "Manager's Special" stickers appear early morning and Sunday evenings.
items: That's when stores clear short-dated inventory.
This one actually can save you money — if you plan to eat it that day.

copy.headline: Grocery store loyalty apps track your purchase history and serve you "personalized deals."
copy.body: In many cases, the tracked price is higher than the untracked shelf price for the same item.

copy.headline: Every pricing trick in the store is optimized around one idea:
items: making you feel like you're saving

copy.headline: We built an app that tracks all of this automatically.
